back: Transfer of thermal energy through a material without the material moving.
Good: metals. Poor (insulators): wood, plastic, wool, air.

front: How does conduction happen in all solids?
back: Particles vibrate more and pass energy to neighbours (lattice vibrations).
Free electrons carry energy quickly through the metal.
Their particles are far apart, so energy is rarely passed on.

front: Why does trapped air insulate well?
back: Air conducts poorly and, when trapped, cannot carry energy by convection.

front: Why does metal feel colder than wood at the same temperature?
back: Metal conducts energy away from your hand faster.
